name: UPPAbaby Cruz V3
price_note: Stroller only; bassinet and Mesa/Aria car seat sold separately. BabyGearLab list $900.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for the Cruz (CPSC title search; recall CSV). UPPAbaby's 2016–2026 recalls cover RumbleSeat adapters (21-158) and the RIDGE jogger (22-215), not the Cruz.
why: Two independent testers agree: BabyGearLab ranks it #1 of 20 full-size strollers (79, Best Full-Size Stroller for Most, Aug 2026) and Wirecutter names it its top pick (Mar 2026). No recall, a single-action colour-coded brake, and a lay-flat seat UPPAbaby rates from birth.
cautions: Not for jogging
Pricey; bassinet is extra
Cannot convert to a double (choose the Vista V3 for that)

name: UPPAbaby Vista V3
price_note: Most colours $999.99 on uppababy.com (one colour $899.99). BabyGearLab lists $1,200; RumbleSeat for double mode is extra.

specs.child_range: Birth with bassinet/SnugSeat, otherwise 3 months–50 lb, up to 40 in

recall_status: No recall of the Vista V3 itself. CPSC 21-158 (Jun 2021): adapters included with UPPAbaby RumbleSeats (the Vista double-mode seat) could detach, about 86,000 units; check older adapters.
why: Ties the Cruz V3 at 79 on BabyGearLab (#2 of 20, High-Quality for Bigger Families) and is Wirecutter's upgrade pick for double strollers; ranked just below the Cruz because of the past RumbleSeat-adapter recall and its larger, heavier frame.
cautions: Large fold; heavy (27.9 lb measured)
Seat alone from 3 months; use bassinet or car seat for newborns
Register RumbleSeat adapters (21-158 recall history)

name: Guava Roam
price_note: List (compare-at) price on guavafamily.com, sold as Roam Stroller & Organizer Bundle; it was on sale for $599.95 in the Sep 3, 2026 snapshot (Labor Day). BabyGearLab list $750. Car-seat adapter extra.

specs.child_range: Seat 6 months–60 lb; from birth only with infant car seat + adapter

recall_status: CPSC 25-032 (Nov 7, 2024): ~8,500 FIRST-GENERATION Roam strollers made July 2020–Dec 2021; brakes can fail to engage or disengage (67 lock-disengage + 152 pedal-not-engaging reports, no injuries); free repair kit. Units made after Dec 2021 are outside the recall, so new current-production units are post-fix; check the date label on used ones.
why: BabyGearLab scores it 72 in its full-size test (#3 of 20, Aug 2026) and names it Best Overall jogger (88), and it praises the single-action colour-coded brakes. It sits below the UPPAbabys because of the 2024 brake recall, which covered only first-generation 2020–21 units, and because the seat starts at 6 months.
cautions: Check the manufacture date on used units: Jul 2020–Dec 2021 = recalled brakes (CPSC 25-032)
Seat from 6 months; newborns need a car seat and adapter
Lower basket limit than rivals (BabyGearLab); 28.4 lb

name: Nuna SWIV
price_note: Base colours $1,000 (some $1,050); includes travel-system adapter. Bassinet sold separately.

specs.child_range: Up to 50 lb (newborn via PIPA car seat or bassinet)

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (CPSC title search for Nuna returns only 2016 high chairs; recall CSV).
why: Consumer Reports' 2026 Top Pick for travel systems is the SWIV + PIPA aire rx, with 'near-perfect ratings' for the stroller in CR's ease-of-use, safety and maneuverability tests; no recall. Ranked below the UPPAbabys and the Guava Roam because only one lab has tested it and CR's numbers are paywalled.
cautions: CR says it 'feels a little heavy and large'
Evidence comes from CR's travel-system test; no BabyGearLab or Wirecutter result
Bassinet extra for newborn lie-flat use
sources: Consumer Reports top picks for travel systems (May 2026)

name: Baby Jogger City Mini GT2
price_note: BabyGearLab list price. babyjogger.com showed the GT2 out of stock on Sep 3, 2026 (archived page); successor City Mini GT3 is on sale but has not been tested by BabyGearLab or Wirecutter.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for Baby Jogger strollers (last stroller recalls 2009–2012).
why: Two labs agree it is a solid pick: Wirecutter's off-road pick and top side-by-side double (GT2 Double), and BabyGearLab 59 (#8 of 20). Clean recall record and a 65 lb limit, but the GT2 is out of stock at Baby Jogger and its GT3 successor is untested.
cautions: Being replaced by the GT3; GT2 out of stock on babyjogger.com
Hand-operated parking brake 'takes some finessing' (BabyGearLab)
Newborn use via car seat adapter; no included bassinet

name: Thule Spring (now Spring 2)
price_note: thule.com now sells the Spring 2 at $499.95; the tested original Spring had a BabyGearLab list price of $500, and Wirecutter (Mar 2026) says it is still available while it tests the Spring 2.

specs.child_range: Seat from 6 months to 64 lb / 44 in (BabyGearLab, original Spring); Spring 2: max 55 lb, from birth with bassinet or car seat + adapter

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for the Spring. Thule's stroller-related recalls in the window are the Sleek handlebar (20-164) and Sleek car-seat adapters (20-096).
why: Wirecutter's easy-fold top pick and BabyGearLab 59 (#9 of 20), with a single-action brake and no recall. Ranked mid-table because the tested original is being replaced by the untested Spring 2, and newborns need an adapter for a car seat.
cautions: Test results are for the original Spring; Spring 2 is untested
Car seat needs an adapter
Wirecutter: harness must be buckled in a fixed order; narrow frame is weaker off-road

name: Nuna MIXX next
price_note: Stroller only; bassinet sold separately. BabyGearLab list $900.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (CPSC title search for Nuna; recall CSV).
why: Tested by two labs (BabyGearLab 62, #6 of 20; Wirecutter 'worth considering'), but both flag stability. With 36 lb aboard, Wirecutter said big bumps 'threatened to tip it over', and BabyGearLab notes a 'possible tip-over risk' off-road, which drops it below the clean two-lab picks.
cautions: Tip-over concern on bumps/rough ground (Wirecutter, BabyGearLab)
Brake-adjacent pocket gets kicked when setting the brake
Small 11 lb basket per BabyGearLab

name: Joie Ginger dlx
price_note: joiebaby.com/us price (archived Jun 6, 2026; live site returns 403 to automated requests). BabyGearLab list $400.
recall_status: None found 2016–2026 (CPSC title search for Joie returned no recalls; not in recall CSV).
why: BabyGearLab's Best Budget full-size stroller, scoring 59 (#7 of 20, Aug 2026). It is usable from birth in pramette mode, has a single-pedal brake and no recall. Only one lab has tested it.
cautions: Brake has no engaged/released colour indicator (BabyGearLab)
Heavy for its class and one of the largest when folded
Only one independent test

name: Cybex Balios S Lux

specs.child_range: Seat 6 months to ~55 lb; from birth with Cybex car seat or cot (sold separately)

recall_status: None found 2016–2026 for Cybex strollers (CPSC 'Cybex' hits are the unrelated fitness firm; Cybex car-seat recalls 23C-001/25C-002 do not involve this stroller).
why: BabyGearLab scores it 64 (#5 of 20) and praises its single-action rocker brake, and it has no recall. But that review dates from March 2024, no second lab has tested it, and the seat starts at 6 months.
cautions: Seat from 6 months (Cybex); newborns need a cot or car seat
Leg rest end is only fabric (BabyGearLab)
Single 2024 test
sources: NHTSA 25C-002 (Aton G seats, not this stroller)

name: Evenflo Pivot Xpand Modular Stroller
price_note: evenflo.com price (archived Sep 3, 2026; live site rate-limits automated requests). A newer Pivot Xpand NXT ($349.99) is also listed and untested.

specs.child_range: Lay-flat carriage mode from birth (Evenflo: 4–55 lb); BabyGearLab: birth–55 lb / 43 in

recall_status: No stroller recall found 2016–2026. NHTSA 25C-003 (Mar 2025) covered some Evenflo seats and travel systems, including 'Gold Pivot Xpand' travel systems, shipped without the recall registration card (labeling only).
why: The labs disagree. Wirecutter's less-expensive top pick ('similar to the Cruz') scored last of 20 at BabyGearLab (46). It has single-action brakes and converts single-to-double, but it is heavy.
cautions: BabyGearLab: lowest score of 20
Heaviest of Wirecutter's picks (30 lb measured); 'not great on rougher surfaces'
Evenflo warranty only 90 days (Wirecutter)
